messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (10 values). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (10 values). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sample t-test assuming equal variances? Usually independent t-test with equal variances? The problem didn't specify. We'll assume equal variances (pooled). Compute means, variances, pooled variance, t-statistic, degrees of freedom = n1+n2-2 = 18. Then compute two-tailed p-value. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27; +18=45; +20=65; +22=87; +25=112; +28=140; +30=170; +32=202; +35=237. Mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute sum of squares: For each value, compute (x - mean)^2.

Compute deviations:

12: diff = -11.7, square = 136.89
15: diff = -8.7, square = 75.69
18: diff = -5.7, square = 32.49
20: diff = -3.7, square = 13.69
22: diff = -1.7, square = 2.89
25: diff = 1.3, square = 1.69
28: diff = 4.3, square = 18.49
30: diff = 6.3, square = 39.69
32: diff = 8.3, square = 68.89
35: diff = 11.3, square = 127.69

Sum of squares = let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10. So sum of squared deviations = 518.10. Sample variance s1^2 = sum/(n-1) = 518.10/9 = 57.5667.

Dataset B: sum = 14+17+19+21+23+26+29+31+33+36 = let's sum: 14+17=31; +19=50; +21=71; +23=94; +26=120; +29=149; +31=180; +33=213; +36=249. Mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Compute deviations:

14: diff = -10.9, square = 118.81
17: diff = -7.9, square = 62.41
19: diff = -5.9, square = 34.81
21: diff = -3.9, square = 15.21
23: diff = -1.9, square = 3.61
26: diff = 1.1, square = 1.21
29: diff = 4.1, square = 16.81
31: diff = 6.1, square = 37.21
33: diff = 8.1, square = 65.61
36: diff = 11.1, square = 123.21

Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. So sum of squared deviations = 478.90. Sample variance s2^2 = 478.90/9 = 53.2111.

Pooled variance sp^2 = [(n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2]/(n1+n2-2) = [9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111]/18 = [518.1003 + 478.8999]/18 = 997.0002/18 = 55.38999. So sp^2 ≈ 55.39. Pooled standard deviation sp = sqrt(55.39) ≈ 7.44.

t-statistic = (mean_A - mean_B)/[sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2)] = (23.7 - 24.9) = -1.2. Denominator: sp * sqrt(1/10 + 1/10) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.44 * 0.4472136 = 3.327. So t = -1.2 / 3.327 = -0.3607. So absolute t = 0.361.

Degrees of freedom = 18. Two-tailed p-value: For t=0.361, df=18. We can approximate using t distribution. t=0.361 is very small; p-value will be large > 0.7. Let's compute approximate p-value: For df=18, t=0.361, p ≈ 0.72? Let's approximate using t distribution table: For df=18, t critical for alpha=0.05 two-tailed is about 2.101. For alpha=0.01 two-tailed is about 2.878. Our t is far less. So p-value > 0.7. Let's compute more precisely using t distribution. We can approximate using normal: t=0.361, df large, p ≈ 2*(1 - Φ(|t|)) where Φ is standard normal CDF. Φ(0.361) ≈ 0.641. So 1-Φ = 0.359. Double gives 0.718. So p ≈ 0.718. So p > 0.05 and > 0.01. So we fail to reject null at both levels.

Thus results: t = -0.361, df=18, p ≈ 0.718. At alpha=0.05, fail to reject. At alpha=0.01, fail to reject.

We need to use the function t_test. Provide dataset_A, dataset_B, alpha=0.05 first, then alpha=0.01. The function returns something. We need to call it twice. Let's do that.
